P.O. Box --- 386.
Sannomiya Post Office.
Kobe. Nov 28th 1922.
D.619
J.F.T. Milne Esq
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

I am in receipt of your letter of the 22th ulto and desire to express
deep regret that circumstances should have arisen to drive me to the course I
was obliged to adopt.

As the whole matter is closed, so far as I personally am concerned there
is no object in setting out at length a recapitulation of the whole unfortunate
circumstances. Sufficient, however, to say that the line of conduct adopted by
Mrs Milne in this matter was utterly contemptible, all the more so in that the
acts perpetrated were against a FRIEND who had always showed her that courtesy and
respect that is due from a man and a gentleman to any lady. My feelings and conduct
towards Mrs Milne have always been XXXX such as I would expect from others towards
my own wife. The taking of the ¥35 was the culmination of many other dirty acts
and it was the "last straw" with me.

I may here say that I am and have always been amazed and completely
dumbfounded as to why she behaved as she did, if it was money that was required
she could most certainly have had a loan of any sum that she temporarily needed
and why she should return to me Yen 200.00 and still retain in her possession the
paltry sum of Yen 150.00 is a complete mystery, unless it is that she considers
that I am in some way indebted to her, and in this event, then she is most
heartily welcome to it and to any further amount which she considers due, BUT,
what it can be for is beyond me to fathom out. Nothing that Mrs Milne has done
can alter the respect, esteem and regard which I entertain for her husband and I
can only (in this last communication) again express my deep and sincere regrets
that she should have, for no reason whatever, broken up a friendship which I
valued.

Yours faithfully.

邮政信箱 --- 386号。
三宫邮局。
神户。1922年11月28日。
D.619
J.F.T. Milne 先生
上海。

尊敬的先生：

我已收到您上月22日的来信，对于迫使我采取上述行动的情况，我深表遗憾。

既然此事就我个人而言已告终结，再详细重述这些不幸的经过已无必要。 suffice it to say（ suffice it to say 意为“ suffice it to say”，此处依语境译为“只需指出”）Milne 夫人在此事中的行为极其卑鄙，尤其令人不齿的是，她的所作所为是针对一位朋友的，而这位朋友始终对她保持着男士和绅士对任何女士应有的礼貌与尊重。我对 Milne 夫人的感受和态度始终是 XXXX，正如我希望别人对待我自己的妻子那样。拿走那35日元是许多其他肮脏行径的顶点，对我而言这是“压垮骆驼的最后一根稻草”。

在此我可以表示，我一直对她为何如此行事感到惊讶且完全目瞪口呆；如果她需要钱，她绝对可以借到任何她暂时需要的金额；而她为何退还我200.00日元，却仍保留那微不足道的150.00日元，这完全是个谜，除非她认为我在某种程度上欠她钱。如果是这样，那么她尽可拿去，以及她认为应付的任何进一步金额，但是，究竟是为了什么，我无法参透。Milne 夫人所做的任何事情都无法改变我对她丈夫的尊重、敬重和关切，我只能（在这最后的通信中）再次表达我深切而真诚的遗憾，因为她毫无理由地破坏了我所珍视的友谊。

此致
敬礼。

KOBE, Japan.
Refer to your No I.O. D 619.
November 25th 1929.

R.C. Alers Esq.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir;-

I am in receipt of your letter dated 11th inst and have also
to acknowledge receipt of the MSS which you have been kind enough to
forward on to me. Please accept my thanks for your efforts in this
unfortunate matter. I have also received a note from Mr. Milne and which
I am acknowledging by this mail.

I am, Dear Sir,
Yours faithfully.
J.H. KERR

PS-- On further thought, before this letter if mailed. I have decided to enclose
herewith for your perusal copy of my note to Mr. Milne. This is done so that
you will see what has passed in this last communication on the subject.

J.H.K.

P,O, Box 386
Sannomiya Post Office.
Kobe.
Nov 5th 1929.

J.C. Aiers Esq.
A/Director of C.I.D. Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

Your letter of the 29th ulto received. I will be obliged if you
will forward the MSS on to me and if refund of postage is required, it
will gladly be sent.

Mrs. Milne is deliberately misleading you when she says that I
told her she might destroy the MSS and it is obviously part of a scheme to
wriggle out of the predicament she has got herself into. I never for one
instant thought the my publishers would have sent the packet to Shanghai
but waited for it at Kobe all these months and the knowledge that she had
made away with this made me desperate.

You are correct in saying that I wrote to her and to Mr. Milne since
she comitted the XXXX acts she did. The reason was that owing to my
high respect for Mr. Milne I was most unwilling to expose her and I was not
sure if the letters I wrote reached her or her husband. However, when I
heard that the MSS in question had gone to Shanghai by mistake I was
frantic with anxiety and much distressed.

I note that you keep discreetly silent on certain significant features
of this case, anyhow, as the MSS has now been recovered I am not disposed t
to go to any further trouble, mainly on account of my feelings for Mr.
Milne but this woman must keep away from me and keep out of my life.

I may add that the British Consulate-General had not yet been advised
of the matter and will not now be informed and the whole affair will drop
so far as I am concerned, that is, unless I am subjected to any further
annoyance.

J.H. Kerr ------------------ Yours faithfully.

邮政信箱 386号
三宫邮局。
神户。
1929年11月5日。

J.C. Aiers 先生
上海刑事调查处代理处长。

尊敬的先生，

已收到您上月29日的来信。如果您能将手稿转寄给我，我将不胜感激；如果需要退还邮费，我很乐意支付。

Milne 夫人声称我曾告诉她可以销毁手稿，这显然是故意误导您，这显然是她为了摆脱自身困境而策划的一部分。我从未想过我的出版商会将包裹寄往上海，而是几个月来一直在神户等待它，得知她已将其处理掉让我感到绝望。

您说得对，自从她犯下那些 XXXX 行径以来，我曾写信给她和 Milne 先生。原因是出于我对 Milne 先生的高度尊重，我非常不愿意揭露她，而且我不确定我写的信是否到达了她或她丈夫手中。然而，当我听说有关的手稿被误寄到上海时，我焦虑得发狂，非常痛苦。

我注意到您对本案某些重要特征保持谨慎的沉默，无论如何，既然手稿现已找回，我不打算再惹更多麻烦，主要是出于我对 Milne 先生的感情，但这个女人必须远离我，退出我的生活。

我可以补充一点，英国总领事馆尚未获悉此事，现在也不会被告知，就我而言，整个事件就此了结，除非我再受到进一步的骚扰。

J.H. Kerr ------------------ 此致
敬礼。

October 29, 29.

J.H. Kerr Esq.
Dear Sir,

In reply to your letters concerning the alleged theft by Mrs. Milne, the wife of Inspector Milne of this Force, I have to inform you that both Mrs. Milne and her husband have been interviewed and the former is very indignant at your allegations which she emphatically denies and produces a letter written by you in which you ask her to order and send clothing to you in Japan. As this letter is dated September 15, 1929 and the alleged theft took place in March last it would appear peculiar that you should ask for certain favour from the lady and then complain after failing to lay a charge for seven months.

In addition I am informed that you have since March been in communication with both Inspector Milne and Mrs. Milne and in none of your letters to the former have you complained of the theft by the latter.

The explanation given by the lady of being in possession of the P.O. Box key is that you personally gave it to her before leaving Shanghai and that she consistently removed the "□□□□□□ World" from it and that you concurred in the action. She also states that you wrote asking her to take the M.S.S. and destroy it as it had been refused by

尊敬的先生，

关于您指控本队督察 Milne 之妻 Milne 夫人盗窃一事，回复您的来信，我须告知您，Milne 夫人及其丈夫均已接受问询，前者对您的指控感到非常愤怒，她坚决否认，并出示了一封您写给她的信，信中您要求她向您订购衣物并寄往日本。由于这封信的日期是1929年9月15日，而所谓的盗窃发生在去年3月，您在七个月内未提出指控，随后却向该女士请求某种通融，这似乎有些奇怪。

此外，我获悉自3月以来，您一直与 Milne 督察和 Milne 夫人保持通信，而在您写给前者的所有信件中，均未投诉后者的盗窃行为。

该女士解释持有邮政信箱钥匙的原因是，您在离开上海前亲自将其交给她，并且她持续从中取出“□□□□□□ World”（原文不清），而您对此表示同意。她还陈述，您写信要求她取走手稿（M.S.S.）并予以销毁，因为出版商已拒绝接收，

Sannomiya Post Office. Kobe.
Sept 13th 1929.

Dear Rachel,

Some time ago I received your letter dated July 4th, however, I as I am not sure if you are once again fooling me I did not send any reply. You have been a bit of a damned fool about that matter of the $ 100.00 allowing such a small thing as that to bust up a warm friendship. No doubt you thought I would send some nasty letter to the old man about it, however, I am not that kind of a man.

If you are still disposed to be friends ( forget all about the past) will you help me in the following small matter. When I was over in Shanghai I arranged for the Chinese tailor in the foreign Y.M.C.A to keep my measure for clothes. I wrote him a week or so ago and got some samples from him and the prices are far away under what I can clothes here in Japan for. I want to get a nice suit of grey flannels, a coat, vest, and TWO pair of trowsers made by him and brought over here by someone who is coming this way. His price is S$60.00 for the lot and that is quite O.K.
$60.00

Let me know, kid, if you could fix this for me. I would probably send over one of my old navy blue suits so that he can cut the new suit to exactly same size. I will arrange for payment by a draft on the H & S. Bank there. Hope you are all O.K. and that the old man is keeping fit and well. I hate this place like Hell and would not hesitate mush to beat it for Shanghai again if a good chance comes along.

Drop me anote.

Yours faithfully.
Jack Sass
page_data.zh:
邮政信箱 ---386号。
三宫邮局。神户。
1929年9月13日。

亲爱的 Rachel，

不久前我收到了你7月4日的来信，但是，因为我不确定你是否又在耍我，所以我没有回复。在那100美元的事情上，你表现得有点像个该死的傻瓜，让这样一件小事破坏了一段温暖的友谊。毫无疑问，你以为我会就此给那个老头子写一封恶毒的信，然而，我不是那种人。

如果你还愿意做朋友（忘记过去的一切），你能否在以下这件小事上帮我一把。我在上海时，安排外国青年会（Y.M.C.A.）的中国裁缝保留了我的衣服尺寸。我在一周左右前给他写了信，并从他那里得到了一些样品，价格远低于我在日本这里做衣服的费用。我想让他做一套漂亮的灰色法兰绒西装，包括上衣、背心和两条裤子，并由顺路过来的人带到这里。他的总价是60.00新加坡元，这完全可以。
$60.00

孩子，告诉我你是否能帮我搞定这件事。我可能会寄去我的一套旧海军蓝西装，以便他能按照完全相同的尺寸裁剪新西装。我会安排通过那里的汇丰银行（H & S. Bank）汇票付款。希望你们一切都好，希望老头子身体健康。我讨厌这个地方如同地狱一般，如果有好机会，我会毫不犹豫地再次溜回上海。

给我写个便条。

此致
敬礼。
Jack Sass

P.O. Box ---- 386, Sannomiya Post Office, Kobe, Japan.
October 22nd 1929.

Copy to--Superintendent Shanghai Post Office
Copy to-- British Consul-General, Shanghai

The Officer Commanding C.I.D.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,
J.H. KERR-- KOBE--JAPAN. COMPLAINT RE MRS, MILNE OF SHANGHAI.
f------------------------------------------------------------

I confirm my letter to you ( registered) of the 9th inst and have to advise
you that I am in receipt of a communication ( No 45748 G.C.D.) from the Shanghai
Post Office telling me that a person named R. Milne handed in to the Post Office on
the 3rd July this year the key for Box No 1425 ( my box) and also the receipt and
signed a voucher as RHH-R. Milne for John Henry Kerr ------------Here is positive proof
of the theft of my wallet in Kobe from my residence and this woman has actually
had the effrontery to return it to the Post Office and obtain $ 5.00 refund through a
forged signature. I enclose herewith for your perusal the original letter from
the Post Office dated 15th inst and ask that you co-operate with the Post Office
authorities in pushing this case against Milne.

In the meantime, I have written to Messrs Herbert Jenkins, Ltd of London
asking them to begin tracing the whereabouts of the Manuscript, the loss of which
I feel so keenly and in due course I will send you further details.

But, in any case, here is positive proof of a criminal act on THE part
of this woman, a crime committed within the jurisdiction of the Municipal Police
and I ask that immediate action be taken against this woman. I am ready to
give evidence on commission at the British Consulate here and if necessary, will
proceed to Shanghai to appear in court against her. Statements can also be taken at
the Consulate from my amah who saw the woman searching my trunk at my house during
my absence. On thinking the whole matter over I am now sure in my own mind that
what she was searching for was letter she sent from the Benin Islands and which might
have compromised her relatives there in regard to the request that I act as an
intermediary for the passing of letters HK which she wanted me to re-address to
Shanghai.

I meanwhile await your advices as to what can be done but trust that it
will be possible to obtain from this woman the missing manuscript which I have
referred to before.

I am, Dear Sir,
Yours very truly.
J. H. Kerr

ENC- Letter No 45748 G.C.D. dated J.H. KERR
15th Oct from Shanghai Post Office

邮政信箱 ---- 386号，三宫邮局，日本神户。
1929年10月22日。

抄送--上海邮政总局主管
抄送--英国驻上海总领事

刑事调查处指挥官
上海。

尊敬的先生，
J.H. KERR-- 神户--日本。 关于上海 Milne 夫人的投诉。
f------------------------------------------------------------

我确认我方本月9日致您的（挂号）信，并须告知您，我已收到上海邮政局的一份通信（编号 45748 G.C.D.），告知我一名名为 R. Milne 的人于今年7月3日向邮局递交了1425号信箱（我的信箱）的钥匙以及收据，并以 RHH-R. Milne 代 John Henry Kerr 的名义签署了一张凭证 ------------ 这是我钱包在神户住所被盗的确凿证据，而这个女人竟然厚颜无耻地将其归还邮局，并通过伪造签名获得了5.00美元的退款。现随函附上邮局本月15日的原始信件供您审阅，并要求您与邮局当局合作，推进针对 Milne 的此案。

与此同时，我已写信给伦敦的 Herbert Jenkins, Ltd 公司，要求他们开始追踪那份令我深感痛惜的手稿的下落，届时我将向您发送更多细节。

但是，无论如何，这里有确凿证据证明这个女人犯下了刑事行为，这是一起在公共租界警务处管辖范围内犯下的罪行，我要求立即对该女人采取行动。我准备在此地的英国领事馆通过委托方式作证，如有必要，我将前往上海出庭控告她。我的阿妈也可以在该领事馆提供证词，她曾目睹该女人在我不在家时搜查我家中的箱子。在仔细思考整件事后，我现在确信她在寻找的是她从贝宁群岛（Benin Islands）寄出的信件，这些信件可能会危及她在那里的亲属，涉及她要求我作为中间人传递信件 HK 的请求，她希望我将这些信件重新地址寄往上海。

我同时等待您关于可以采取何种措施的建议，但相信有可能从这个女人那里追回我之前提到的遗失手稿。

尊敬的先生，
此致
最诚挚的敬礼。

Hongkew Police Station.
File Record No. 2176.

CONTINUATION
SHEET
Confidential.

Sir,

Letter from J.H. Kerr,
Kobe, re Mrs. R. Milne.

The attached letter was received through the
Post at Hongkew Station on October 14, 1929. I opened
same before realising it was not actually addressed to
Hongkew.
Inquiries made at the C.P.O. elicit that P.O.
Box No. 1425 was rented by John Henry Kerr on the 8th.,
October 1928, who paid the usual deposit of $5.00. This
deposit is refunded on the key of the box being returned
in good order. On July 3, 1929, the key of the above box
was returned to the Postal Authorities who duly refunded
the $5.00 deposit. The receipt for this refund is signed
"K (or R.) Milne for John Henry Kerr". This receipt and
a letter from Kerr are in the hands of the Postal Authori-
ties. Kerr in his letter (dated 9/10/29) to the Postal
Authorities states that on the 23rd March 1929, a foreign
woman, under the influence of drink, visited his house in
Kobe during his absence. Kerr's amah saw this woman whilst
in the house search his (Kerr's) trunk. When he Kerr
examined his effects on hearing this story from the amah,
he discovered Y300.00 and certain papers and a bunch of
keep including the key of P.O. Box 1425 missing.
The next day he located Mrs. Milne in the
Tanakaya hotel (Kobe) and accused her of stealing the
articles mentioned. She admitted to him visiting his
house in a drunken fit but denied the stealing. He, did
not expect that any more mail matter would be delivered
to the Shanghai P.O. Box and dropped the whole matter, not
even advising the P.O. re loss of Box Key.
About 2 months after this (sometime in May) he
wrote to Mrs. Milne in Shanghai threatening exposure to
her husband and to the Police if she did not return the
stolen property. About 10 days after sending this letter
he received advice from the Hongkong and Shanghai Banking
Corporation that R. Milne had remitted to him Y200.00 from
the Hongkew Branch of the Hongkong & Shanghai Bank Corp.,
In view of the money being returned he concludes
Mrs. Milne the party guilty of the larceny from his house
in March last, and the P.O. Box Key being returned on
3/7/29, to the Postal Authorities, and the receipt for the
refund being signed "R. Milne" seems to verify his susp-
icions.
As regards the loss of the MSS sent by Messrs.
Herbert Jenkins, London to Kerr at the PO. Box 1425 the
Postal Authorities here cannot trace the Registered receipt
without the number, which can only be obtained from Messrs.
Jenkins. They have written Kerr to this effect telling
him to write London for the Registered receipt number and
send same to them when they can trace the receipt issued
here.
J.H.Kerr was on the staff of the "Shanghai
Mercury" for a few months (1928-1929) and whilst here was
on intimate terms with Mrs. Milne. From what I can gather,
he had not a savoury reputation.

Yours Obediently,

先生，

来自神户 J.H. Kerr 关于 R. Milne 夫人的信函。

附件中的信件于1929年10月14日通过虹口巡捕房的邮局收到。我在意识到它实际上并非寄给虹口巡捕房之前拆开了它。
向中央邮局查询后得知，第1425号邮政信箱由 John Henry Kerr 于1928年10月8日租用，他支付了常规的5.00美元押金。当信箱钥匙完好归还时，该押金予以退还。1929年7月3日，上述信箱的钥匙被归还给邮政当局，后者 duly 退还了5.00美元押金。这笔退款的收据签署为“K（或 R.）Milne 代 John Henry Kerr”。该收据以及 Kerr 的一封信件均在邮政当局手中。Kerr 在给邮政当局的信（日期为1929年10月9日）中称，1929年3月23日，一名外国女子在醉酒状态下，趁他不在家时造访了他在神户的住所。Kerr 的女佣看到这名女子在屋内翻查他（Kerr）的手提箱。当 Kerr 从女佣处听到此事并检查他的财物时，发现300日元、某些文件以及一串钥匙（包括第1425号邮政信箱的钥匙）失踪。
第二天，他在田中屋旅馆（神户）找到了 Milne 夫人，并指控她偷窃了上述物品。她承认曾醉酒后造访他的住所，但否认偷窃。他预计不会再有邮件投递到上海的邮政信箱，因此未再追究此事，甚至未就信箱钥匙丢失一事通知邮局。
大约两个月后（五月某时），他写信给在上海的 Milne 夫人，威胁说如果她不归还被盗财物，就将向其丈夫和警方揭露此事。发出这封信约10天后，他收到汇丰银行的通知，称 R. Milne 已从汇丰银行虹口分行向他汇款200日元。鉴于款项已退回，他断定 Milne 夫人就是去年三月从他家中行窃的罪犯，而邮政信箱钥匙于1929年7月3日归还给邮政当局，且退款收据由“R. Milne”签署，这似乎证实了他的怀疑。
至于赫伯特·詹金斯公司（伦敦）寄给 Kerr 并存入第1425号邮政信箱的手稿丢失一事，此地的邮政当局在没有编号的情况下无法追踪挂号收据，该编号只能从詹金斯公司获得。他们已就此致信 Kerr，告知他向伦敦方面索取挂号收据编号，并在收到后发送给他们，以便他们在此地追踪发出的收据。
J.H. Kerr 曾在《上海泰晤士报》（Shanghai Mercury）任职数月（1928-1929年），在此期间他与 Milne 夫人关系亲密。据我所知，他的名声并不好。

卑职，

A区警司 R. [签名] 督察

----------------------------------------

I am a British subject and was formerly a resident of
Shanghai and am at present the renter of P.O. Box 1425-Shanghai Post
Office.
It is with the greatest urgency and haste that I have to
advise you that mail matter is being stolen from the above P.O. Box
because of the theft of the key of same. The key of this box was
stolen from my room at ███ my residence by a woman named Rachel
Milne of 574 Dixwell Road, the key was taken amongst other property
amongst which was an envelope containing Japanese bank notes to the
value of Yen 300.00

I have just received a letter from Messrs Herbert Jenkins, Ltd
of 3 York Street. Saint James's. London., saying that on the 1st Feb
this year they mailed to me at my Post Box 1425 at Shanghai a very
valuable MSS ( of great value to me but only so much waste paper to
anyone else) and I have now reason to believe that this MSS has been
obtained from the Shanghai Post Office by the woman ---Milne---
mentioned above, by forging my signature on a Post Office receipt for

#- Superintendent of Shanghai Post Office.

The Officer Commanding C.I.D.
Shanghai.

Dear Sir,

In further connection with my communication dated 7th inst. I should add that the packet containing the MSS which I referred to was sent to Shanghai REGISTERED and it will be an easy matter to trace it.

An outline of the whole affair is as follows--I was in Shanghai up to 4th Jan this year and was subjected to considerable annoyance from the woman--Milne----( of 574 Dixwell Road) through her ridiculous attentions to me, which I did not want, knowing her character. Well, I came to Kobe on the 7th Jan this year and was living at a private Hotel known as the Hankyu House Pension and, to my great astonishment, the woman-Milne- suddenly presented herself at the Pension and asked for me. She insisted on staying there, together with a small boy-- an adopted son, I believe. She said that she was going down to the Bonin Islands on some private business. After a time of much embarrassment to me, owing to her disgraceful behaviour in the Pension, she left for the Bonin Islands.

I meanwhile, left the Pension and rented a house and went to live in it. Whilst in the Bonin Islands Milne wrote me three letters and in the last one she said that she would come to see me on her passing through Kobe, as she had something to tell me and that she wanted me to do a certain favour for her and her relatives. I was completely mystified at what she was driving at.

Anyhow, it was one night, I think about the 23rd of March that I came home from my office and my amah was in an agitated state and told me that a foreign woman had walked into my house that morning and said that she would wait for me to return that night. She was slightly under the influence of liquor, the amah said. The amah also told me that about an hour after the woman came into my room she ( the amah) suddenly walked in to the room and caught her in the act of going through my trunk, with a lot of my private papers lying about. On hearing this I rushed to a leather grip which had contained my wallet with an envelope which held Japanese bank notes to the value of a trifle over Yen 300.00 and other property including a contract relating to employment from a Japanese firm. Letters from Ireland, an old and useless Letter of Credit on the New York Branch of the Yokohama Specie Bank, some photos, a large bunch of keys and also the key of Shanghai Post Office Box 1435 attached to which was a large white label with the written characters Shanghai No---4655. ( this was attached by me whilst in your city as a measure of safety in case it was lost). Everything was GONE. I instantly went to the Hankyu House to ask if the woman Milne had returned there. They said NO.

It was next day that I located Milne in a Japanese Hotel ( the Tsuchiya Hotel) and accused her of stealing the things I have above referred to. She indignantly denied it and said that she had come to my house in a drunken fit but that she had not stayed and HAD NOT GOT ANYTHING HERE TO DO WITH ME. Knowing that it was a hundred to one chance that she had thrown away the property that might have been identified, I reluctantly abandoned the whole matter and as I did not expect that any more mail would be delivered to the Shanghai Post Office Box, I went to no further trouble about advising the Post Office People about the theft of the key. Also, I had met this woman's husband and it was in some measure out of respect for his feelings that I decided to take no further steps against the woman.

#- 上海邮局总监。

上海刑事侦缉处指挥官。

尊敬的先生，

就我本月7日的通信进一步补充说明，我提到的包含手稿的邮包是作为挂号信寄往上海的，因此追踪它将是一件容易的事。

整个事件的概要如下--直到今年1月4日我都在上海，期间受到名为 --Milne----（住址狄思威路574号）的女子的严重骚扰，她对我表现出荒谬的关注，而我鉴于她的品行，并不想要这种关注。好吧，我于今年1月7日来到神户，住在一家名为阪急之家公寓（Hankyu House Pension）的私人旅馆里，令我大为惊讶的是，该女子 -Milne- 突然出现在公寓并找我。她坚持要住在那里，还带着一个小男孩--我相信是养子。她说她要去小笠原群岛处理一些私人事务。由于她在公寓里的可耻行为让我尴尬了一段时间后，她前往小笠原群岛。

与此同时，我离开了公寓，租了一所房子并搬进去住。当 Milne 在小笠原群岛时，她给我写了三封信，在最后一封信中她说，当她途经神户时会来看我，因为她有事要告诉我，并且希望我为她和她的亲戚帮个忙。我对她的意图完全感到困惑。

总之，我想大约是3月23日的一个晚上，我从办公室回家，我的女佣情绪激动，告诉我那天早上有一个外国女人走进我家，说她会等我当晚回来。女佣说她有点喝醉了。女佣还告诉我，在那女人进入我的房间大约一小时后，她（女佣）突然走进房间，当场抓住她正在翻查我的手提箱，我的许多私人文件散落在周围。听到这个消息，我冲到一个皮制手提包里，里面原本装着我的钱包，钱包里有一个信封，装着价值略超过300日元的日本银行券，以及其他财产，包括一份与日本公司的雇佣合同。来自爱尔兰的信件，一张横滨正金银行纽约分行的陈旧且无用的信用证，一些照片，一大串钥匙，以及附有一个写有字符“上海 No---4655”的大白标签的上海第1435号邮政信箱钥匙。（这是我在贵市时为了防止丢失而采取的安全措施附上的）。所有东西都不见了。我立刻去阪急之家询问 Milne 女子是否回到那里。他们说没有。

第二天，我在一家日本旅馆（土屋旅馆）找到了 Milne，并指控她偷窃了我上面提到的物品。她愤怒地否认，说她是在醉酒状态下来到我家，但她没有停留，也与我没有任何关系。我知道她扔掉可能被识别的财物的几率是百分之一，我不情愿地放弃了整件事，而且由于我不指望再有邮件投递到上海邮政信箱，我也没再费心通知邮局人员钥匙被盗之事。此外，我曾见过这个女人的丈夫，出于对他感情的某种尊重，我决定不对该女子采取进一步行动。

page_data.en:
2 w.

I ask you to please note carefully the following curious and significant events. About
EZ two months after she returned to Shanghai from Kobe I was one day thinking and
worrying over my loss when I decided that I would take a chance of writing her a letter
and threatening exposure to her husband and to the Police authorities if she did not
RETURN MY PROPERTY THAT SHE HAD STOLEN. I was considerably astonished about ten days later
to receive a notification from the Hong Kong & Shanghai Bank saying that---

" R. Milne had remitted me Yen 200.00 ( Two hundred only) from the
Hongkow Branch of the H. & S. Bank"

That was all, not a scrap of writing of any kind. I put it to you that unless there
was guilt and the fear of exposure, that this woman Milne would NOT have done this. Why
she did not sent the whole Yen 300.00 I do not know but I am POSITIVE that there was
over Yen 300.00 in the envelope that she stole from my house in Kobe.

Now, as for the really urgent affair in this most unfortunate business-- I was
urgently awaiting the return of a most valuable manuscript from Messrs Herbert Jenkins,
Ltd, for correction and additions and I had instructed Jenkins to send it to KOBE to my
address here. I waited all the time since February right up to a few days ago for it
and there was no sign of it arriving. Then I wrote Jenkins by registered mail and to my
great distress and astonishment, I find that they had mailed it to Shanghai to my
P.O. Box there. I am positive that it has been obtained by means of a forged signature
forged
by this woman--Milne. I should here also mention that when I went to the Tanakaya Hotel
to find her on her return to Kobe from the Bonin Islands, I ascertained that what she
wanted me to do for her was to act as an intermediary for the passing on to Shanghai of
certain letters which she said would be addressed to Kobe by one--Mrs. Kate Washington in
Chichijima in the Bonin Islands. It did not take me very long to arrive at the conclusion
that THIS WOMAN WAS ENGAGED IN ESPIONAGE against the Japanese Naval authorities and I
emphatically declined to do anything in the way she suggested. This latter, is not of any
interest to the Shanghai Police, nor is the theft of the Post Box key ( in Japan) an
offence against the laws of China--BUT--- the forging of my signature and thus obtaining
possession of a postal packet at the Shanghai Post Office IS AN OFFENCE that concerns you
and the Chinese Government. The MSS in question is of the greatest value to me and it
is only so much waste paper to anyone else. It was the manuscript of a novel that was to
be published in London. I most urgently ask that steps be taken to recover it. If you
find that it has been obtained from the Post Office by the woman and that she WILL NOT
produce it, I ask that proceedings be taken. I am ready to give evidence here on a
commission at the British Consulate and will proceed to Shanghai to appear against her
if she is arrested.

As stated before, I am a British subject, an author and knew this woman when she was
inmate of a brothel in Kobe. I enclose herewith for your perusal the following documents,

1--Advice from the H & S Bank that Milne had sent me Yen 200.00
2--Note from Bank acknowledging my request for Milne's address.
3--Letter ( original) addressed to me under date of July 4th by the woman--Milne--
reading as follows,
"Dear Jacky, July 4st 1939.
So sorry I havent answer any of your letters. But I have been in big
trouble & I couldnt do it. If I write I know what will happen.
I am coming to Japan soon & and will tell you all about it. So dont
get angry. I will explain everything. Write to as every thing is clear
now to the house. Well by by.
I will write tomorrow as I have no time.
Yours as ever
BILL
Write soon and let me know if I can come to Kobe or not you know.
Ileen is fine baby as they call her. //"

2 w.

请仔细留意以下离奇且意味深长的事件。在 EZ 从神户返回上海约两个月后，有一天，我正为我的损失而思虑焦虑，于是决定冒险给她写一封信，威胁说如果她不归还她偷走的我的财产，我就向她丈夫和警方当局揭露此事。大约十天后，我收到汇丰银行（Hong Kong & Shanghai Bank）的通知，令我颇为惊讶，通知称——

“R. Milne 已从汇丰银行虹口分行向我汇来日元 200.00 元（仅贰佰元整）”

仅此而已，没有任何只言片语。我想向诸位指出，除非出于内疚和对暴露的恐惧，否则这个名叫 Milne 的女人绝不会这样做。至于她为何没有汇回全部的 300.00 日元，我不得而知，但我确信她在神户从我家中偷走的信封里装有超过 300.00 日元的款项。

现在，谈谈这件极不幸之事中真正紧迫的部分——我当时正急切等待赫伯特·詹金斯有限公司（Messrs Herbert Jenkins, Ltd）寄回一份极其珍贵的手稿，以便进行校正和增补，我曾指示詹金斯将手稿寄至我在神户的上述地址。自二月起直至几天前，我一直在等待，却未见其踪影。随后，我通过挂号信致函詹金斯，令我极度苦恼和震惊的是，我发现他们竟将手稿寄往了上海我的邮政信箱。我确信，这是该女子——Milne——通过伪造签名获取的。在此我还须提及，当她从小笠原群岛返回神户时，我去田中屋酒店（Tanakaya Hotel）找她，得知她希望我充当中间人，将某些信件转递至上海，她说这些信件将由小笠原群岛父岛（Chichijima）的一位凯特·华盛顿夫人（Mrs. Kate Washington）寄往神户。我不久便得出结论，此女正从事针对日本海军当局的间谍活动，因此我断然拒绝按她的建议行事。后一事与上海警方无关，在日本盗窃邮政信箱钥匙也不构成违反中国法律之罪行——但是——伪造我的签名并从而在上海邮局领取邮件包裹，则是关乎贵方及中国政府之罪行。涉案手稿对我而言价值连城，对他人而言不过是一堆废纸。那是一部拟在伦敦出版的小说的手稿。我恳请采取步骤追回该手稿。若查明该女子已从邮局取得手稿且拒不交出，我请求提起诉讼。我准备在英国领事馆通过委托程序在此作证，若其被捕，我将前往上海出庭指控她。

如前所述，我是英国臣民，一名作家，在该女子尚在神户一家妓院为妓时便认识她。现随函附上以下文件供阅：

1-- 汇丰银行通知，称 Milne 已向我汇款 200.00 日元
2-- 银行回复我查询 Milne 地址请求的回执。
3-- 该女子——Milne——于 7 月 4 日写给我的原件信函，内容如下：
“亲爱的 Jacky，1939 年 7 月 4 日。
很抱歉我没有回复你的任何信件。但我遇到了大
麻烦，没法写。如果我写信，我知道会发生什么。
我很快就要去日本了，会把一切都告诉你。所以别
生气。我会解释一切。既然家里现在一切都清楚了，
就写信到家里吧。好吧，再见。
我明天再写，因为我现在没时间。
永远属于你的
BILL
尽快回信，让我知道我能否去神户，你知道的。
Ileen 很好，他们都叫她宝贝。//”

I would like to state that whilst in Shanghai I met Mr. Milne, this woman's husband and
Milne is in every respect a ----Gentleman---- a man who has been most unfortunate in
an alliance with a woman of this type, and on his account, I would have dropped the
whole business had it not been for her dastardly action in stealing mail matter from my
P.O. Box. I urgently request that you will assist me in the recovery of this manuscript,
the loss of the remaining Yen 100.00 is to me a detail and the other things taken are of
little or no value and can be forgotten.

I also enclose herewith ████████████████ No4-- being a letter from Jenkins of
London in which they advise me that the manuscript in question was mailed to
me by registered packet on the 8st Feb. Their letter is dated 10th Sept.

This means that the packet in question was received in Shanghai about the █████████/
20th February this year and should thus be easily traced.

Awaiting with interest and anxiety f your further advices.

I am, Dear Sir,
Yours very truly.

J.H. KERN John H. Kern
page_data.zh:
3.
我愿声明，我在上海期间曾见过 Milne 先生，即该女子的丈夫。Milne 在任何方面都是一位----绅士----，与这种类型的女子结合是他极大的不幸。若非她做出从我的邮政信箱窃取邮件这种卑鄙行径，看在他的份上，我本会放弃整件事。我恳请贵方协助我追回这份手稿，其余 100.00 日元的损失对我而言只是细枝末节，其他被窃物品价值甚微或毫无价值，可以忽略不计。

另随函附上 ████████████████ 第 4 号——即伦敦詹金斯公司（Jenkins）的来信，信中告知我，涉案手稿已于 2 月 8 日通过挂号包裹寄给我。该信日期为 9 月 10 日。

这意味着涉案包裹大约于今年 2 月 █████████/20 日左右抵达上海，因此应易于追踪。

焦急而关切地等候您的进一步消息。

此致，
敬礼。

J.H. KERN John H. Kern
